title: Regression: Modo navigation (Alt) conflicts with CSG symmetrical scaling modifier in 4.7 stable; triggers both simultaneously
body:
### Tested versions

4.7.stable

### System information

Linux (Ubuntu 20.04) - Dedicated graphics card (NVIDIA)

### Issue description

In Godot 4.7 stable, using the Modo 3D viewport navigation scheme (which utilizes Alt for camera orbiting) creates an input handling conflict when modifying a CSG mesh (CSGBox3D, etc.).

When a CSG node is active and you hold Alt while dragging a gizmo handle to perform a symmetrical scale (scaling both sides evenly), the engine correctly triggers the scale modification but fails to consume the event. As a result, the input bleeds through to the viewport canvas, causing the camera to simultaneously orbit/rotate while the mesh is being scaled.

This worked flawlessly in 4.6.3.stable, where holding Alt while manipulating a selected CSG handle cleanly executed the symmetrical scaling modifier and completely suppressed viewport camera navigation. The issue appears to be an input event-handling regression introduced during the recent 3D editor/tool-gizmo input system refactoring.

### Steps to reproduce

Go to Editor Settings > Editors > 3D and set the Navigation Scheme to Modo (where Alt + LMB Drag orbits the camera).

Create a new 3D scene and add any CSG primitive (e.g., a CSGBox3D).

Select the CSG node in the Scene tree to make its red/green/blue viewport handle gizmos visible.

Click and hold one of the handle dots to prepare to scale it.

Hold down the Alt key (the modifier key to scale both sides equally).

Drag the mouse.

Observed Behavior: The mesh scales symmetrically, but the 3D viewport camera also simultaneously spins rapidly around the focus point.

Expected Behavior (as in 4.6.3): The mesh should scale symmetrically, and the viewport camera rotation should be blocked/suppressed while a gizmo handle is actively being manipulated.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - This is a purely editor-side UI/input routing regression that can be reproduced in any blank project by toggling the Modo navigation scheme.
